answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each node to a Wesolowski VDF whose evaluation requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings: every result depends on the previous one, so a clone cannot reduce its own delay by distributing that chain across GPUs. Simulated identities therefore multiply elapsed computation and hardware cost rather than providing cheap parallel capacity, creating a physical sybil bottleneck—like plume over quartz beside a river.
